title: AI Development Manager - Provider Status v0.1
description: Provider-neutral schema for AI quota/usage status. Derived from real PoC evidence (Codex app-server, Claude statusline/JSONL, Antigravity manual, Gemini manual) - does not assume any provider has a fixed set of windows (e.g. five_hour + weekly). Windows are an open list; any window may be absent or null.

generated_at.description: When this status document was assembled (not per-provider last_updated, which lives inside each provider entry).

display_name.description: Human-readable label for UI/report use, e.g. "Codex", "Claude Code", "Antigravity", "Gemini App / Google AI Pro".

collection_mode.description: How this provider's data currently gets into this document. Not a promise that automatic collection is implemented yet - see source_type/confidence for that.

source.description: Concrete mechanism, e.g. "official_app_server" (Codex account/rateLimits/read), "official_statusline", "claude_code_jsonl", "manual_report". Free text, provider-specific vocabulary lives in docs/QUOTA-SOURCES.md.

source_type.description: official = came from the provider's own authoritative API/protocol (e.g. Codex app-server, Claude official statusline rate_limits). local_estimate = derived locally from token/session logs, not authoritative (e.g. claude-monitor JSONL fallback). manual = a human (or an AI acting on a human's report) entered it.

confidence.description: Free-text confidence label carried from the source tool when available (e.g. claude-monitor's "local_estimate"/"official"), or "manual" / "unknown" otherwise. Not constrained to a fixed enum because different upstream tools use different vocabularies.

last_updated.description: When this provider's data was actually captured/reported - NOT when this document was generated. Stale last_updated must not be treated as a live value by any consumer (e.g. ChatGPT dispatch logic).

status.description: Coarse human status. For manual providers (Antigravity, Gemini v0.1) this is the primary signal: abundant | normal | low | exhausted | unknown. For automatic providers this may be derived from windows[] instead of set directly.

windows.description: Zero or more quota windows. Deliberately an open list, not fixed fields - e.g. Codex (this account) has exactly one 7-day window with no secondary; Claude Code may have five_hour and/or seven_day, either of which may be missing independently. Consumers must not assume any specific window name is present.

metadata.description: Source-specific extra fields that don't fit the generic shape, e.g. Codex's planType/credits/spendControlReached, or Antigravity's raw manual note text. Freeform, not validated by this schema.

window.description: A single quota window. All fields except name are individually nullable/optional because different providers/accounts return different subsets (e.g. Codex's real response had primary.usedPercent/windowDurationMins/resetsAt but secondary: null entirely).

name.description: Source-provided or source-derived label, e.g. "primary", "secondary", "five_hour", "seven_day". Not a controlled vocabulary - do not hardcode expectations around specific names.

duration_minutes.description: Window length in minutes if known, e.g. 10080 for a 7-day window (real Codex value). Null if unknown.

resets_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp, or null if unknown/not applicable.
